evidence: RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306).
implication: Per-gene correlation with a single noisy reading is bounded well below 1; scores must be read against a noise ceiling, and validating against smoothed or full-depth targets overstates accuracy.

evidence: The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma).
implication: Rare populations contribute little to a pooled correlation and are easy to underfit; within-cluster correlation should be reported alongside the pooled one.

evidence: 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test.
implication: Gene-level claims need false-discovery-rate control across all in-scope genes.

evidence: The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.
implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.

evidence: ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032.
implication: Report a depth-only baseline; a predictor must beat it before its signal is called biological.

evidence: Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194.
implication: Most predictable variation is cell identity. A plan answers the question only through what it predicts beyond the cluster-mean baseline, gene by gene, on the same cells.

evidence: With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored).
implication: Significance against zero is nearly automatic and cannot be the headline; effect size and the comparison with the cell-type baseline carry the conclusion.
